newsitem.title: INDIA: I-Sec's Indian funds inflow/outflow chart for May.
newsitem.headline: I-Sec's Indian funds inflow/outflow chart for May.

text.p: The following is a table and commentary on the Indian banking system's inflow and outflow of funds in May 1997 compiled by the debt research team of ICICI Securities & Finance Company.
The total inflows in the second fortnight of May are in the region of 38,000 million rupees, and, correspondingly the outflows estimated at 5,500 million rupees are relatively low.
Coupon payments on federal and state government securities in the next fortnight amount to over 26,000 million rupees.

Given the total central and state government securities outstanding of 2,280 billion rupees and an average coupon rate of 10.50 percent on these securities, the average coupon payments are 9,500 million rupees per fortnight making the second half of May distinctly above the average.
Apart from these inflows, any forex intervention by the Reserve Bank to mop up dollars will further augment the surplus funds position.
The large net inflow expected over the next fortnight will significantly add to the liquidity in the system putting a downward pressure on call money rates.
The gilts market, which has been flat for the last couple of weeks with secondary volumes taking a plunge, will see increased activity over the next fortnight.
The maturity spread between two year and five year government securities has widened to 70 basis points and some tightening of this spready is likely to be seen shortly.
Also, the Reserve Bank may announce the next bond issue towards end of May or in early June, and most probably the offering will be a short dated security.
